clue.text: Rodent behind a seat in church somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: the clue puts the run of rodent-behind-a-seat in the church abbreviation, so those letters sit inside
behind means the rodent comes after the seat in the run of letters

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in a church
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rat scurries behind a pew in some Scottish kirk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' and 'in' are the placement words. Cape Wrath is the headland at the far north-west tip of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Wrath is a headland in Sutherland, a place in the far north-west of Scotland.

clue.text: Name of girl to be found in chronicle's entry

indicators.note: to be found in something is to be placed within it, so the verb goes inside the record

parts.note: an annal is a single year's record, an entry in a chronicle
the verb to be gives BE

explanation.surface: A girl's name turns up in a record kept in some chronicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the name is written plainly in a chronicle; 'found in' is the container signal, and a single chronicle entry is one year's record.
explanation.definitionFit: Annabel is a female given name, so it names a girl.

clue.text: See half of them black old ship in restrictive action at port

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two letters, here its second half

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at half the old black ships held in harbour by a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting you to look; 'half of' takes the last two letters of 'them', EM.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on ships leaving or entering a country's ports, a restriction on trade.

clue.text: Old fugitive has to flee, coming to a barrier

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a gate is a barrier across an opening

explanation.surface: An escapee from long ago bolts and reaches a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Runagate is an archaic word for a runaway or vagabond, someone on the run.

clue.text: Community of females, about 50, in new York district

indicators.note: about means the women's quarters go round the number, enclosing it

parts.note: a harem is the women of a household living together
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Some fifty women living together in a part of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The lowercase 'new' is just the surface; 'about' puts L (50) inside HAREM.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem is a neighbourhood in northern Manhattan, part of New York City.

clue.text: Card game in a Suffolk town

explanation.surface: A card game being played in a town in Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk is a county in eastern England; Newmarket there is famous for horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a gambling game played with cards and matching stakes; the other is the English racing town in Suffolk.

clue.text: Old soldier offering prayer, only half in expectation

indicators.note: in means half the prayer is placed within the word for expectation

parts.note: hope is expectation of something good

indicators.note: only half of a six-letter word is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: a litany is a form of prayer with responses

explanation.surface: An old soldier says only half a prayer, in hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' trims a synonym of prayer to its first three letters, and 'in' is the container signal. A hoplite was a heavily armed foot soldier of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoplite was an armoured infantryman in ancient Greek city-states, a warrior of antiquity.

clue.text: Sue, Amanda — naughty to the point where you get fed up?

definitions.text: to the point where you get fed up

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving letters that will not stay in order

explanation.surface: Two badly behaved girls, Sue and Amanda, drive someone to exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges SUE and AMANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is Latin for 'to the point of sickness', said of something repeated until tiresome.

clue.text: Emperor needs outside help — an indication of pressure

indicators.note: the help needs to be outside, wrapping round the emperor

parts.note: aid is help
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An emperor requires external assistance under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs outside' is the container signal: the help wraps the emperor. An aneroid is a barometer that works without liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: An aneroid barometer is an instrument showing atmospheric pressure by a dial.

clue.text: I get hold of daughter, outside home having problems

indicators.note: outside means the run of I, grabbing and daughter goes round the word for home

parts.note: to nab is to get hold of or seize
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone grabs their daughter outside the house and is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the whole run of I, the grab word and daughter round home, so the home word ends up between the grab word and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a bind is an idiom for being stuck in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Layer of fabric everyone turned over

parts.note: lamé is a fabric woven with metallic threads

indicators.note: turned over means the word for everyone is read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A layer of cloth that everybody flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' is the reversal signal; lamé is a shiny fabric with metal threads woven in.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamella is a thin plate or layer, as in the gills of fungi or bone tissue.

clue.text: Birth in Lincoln — does that make one an Australian?!

indicators.note: in puts the word for birth inside the president's first name

parts.note: Abe was US President Abraham Lincoln's familiar name
birth is origin, where something begins

explanation.surface: Asks whether being born in Lincoln makes you a native Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city; it is President Abraham Lincoln by his nickname, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aborigine is one of the original native peoples of Australia.

clue.text: Little girl eastern fellows set up as a goddess

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sis is a little sister
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Some men and a girl from the east raise a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses SIS E MEN as a whole; SIS reads the same both ways. Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek deity of divine vengeance, a female divinity.

clue.text: Girl keeps watch perhaps when this retired don returns

annotationWithheld.why: Girl keeps watch perhaps when this retired don returns (8): SUE keeping TIMER, reversed, gives EREMITUS not EMERITUS; no parse found yields the answer
annotationWithheld.clue: Girl keeps watch perhaps when this retired don returns

clue.text: Female writer occupying rural cottage

indicators.note: a writer occupying the words is lodged inside them, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A woman author lives in a country cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' signals the letters inside 'ruRAL COTTage'. Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was an American novelist, author of Little Women.

clue.text: Tree mammal given to an Oxford museum

parts.note: the ash is a tree
a mole is a small burrowing mammal

explanation.surface: A tree and a stuffed mole are donated to an Oxford museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashmolean is Oxford University's museum of art and archaeology.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean is the university museum of art and archaeology in Oxford, Britain's oldest public museum.

clue.text: Military vessel in port so terribly trendy

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly scrambled

parts.note: hip means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A warship in harbour is dreadfully fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges PORT SO into TROOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A troopship is a ship for carrying soldiers, a vessel of the armed forces.

clue.text: Earnings in respect of ground hosting match

parts.note: re means concerning or in respect of
a venue is the ground where a match is held

explanation.surface: Takings from the stadium where the game is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, the money a business or state takes in.

clue.text: Leading American band entertaining ambassador

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so the ambassador sits within

parts.note: a ring is a band, as worn on a finger
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A US band hosts an ambassador and takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' is the container signal: the ambassador's title lands between the American and the band. His Excellency is the formal style of an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushering means guiding or showing someone the way, as an usher does.

clue.text: A bogus journalist is conscience-stricken

parts.note: a sham is something fake or bogus
ed, an editor, is a crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A fake reporter feels guilty about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ashamed is to feel guilt or embarrassment, troubled by conscience.

clue.text: Continuous flow of lots of pieces of paper on the street

indicators.note: on means the paper is placed after the street abbreviation

parts.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A steady flood of litter lying on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a steady current, as of water or of traffic.

clue.text: Is aware of each learner in upward progress

indicators.note: in places the each-and-learner pair inside the word for upward progress

parts.note: a rise is upward movement or progress
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner on the way up knows what each step means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'upward progress' looks like part of the surface but is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it or understand it.

clue.text: Fancy red coat in a 20s or 30s style

indicators.note: fancy as a verb suggests letters dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An ornate red coat in the fashion of the interwar years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges RED COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric design style popular in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Girl I found outside our place in 28

indicators.note: found outside means girl-and-I go round the possessive word

parts.note: miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A girl is found outside her home in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found outside' is the container signal. The cross-reference 28 points to the country solved at 28-across, where Missouri is a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is a US state, a place in the country solved at 28.

clue.text: Opening with a pound as amount to be paid

parts.note: a rent is a tear or gap, an opening
L stands for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A slot advertised with a pound as the fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is the sum paid to rent something, a hire charge.

clue.text: English parts one translated into a different language

indicators.note: translated suggests the words being changed into another form

explanation.surface: English sections, the first rendered into another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' is the anagram signal, applied to 'parts one' only; 'into' is a link and the English abbreviation stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: One telling fibs endlessly is operating in a secret affair

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for a fibber is cut

parts.note: a liar is someone telling fibs
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: A habitual fibber is conducting a clandestine romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LIAR to LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a sexual relationship, especially an illicit one kept hidden.

clue.text: Fur dress with hem above the knee, very short

parts.words: dress with hem above the knee
parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt or dress

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

explanation.surface: A fur garment worn with a very short dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims VERY to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniver is white fur, used for trimming ceremonial robes.

clue.text: A maiden sitting by the heather in the country

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
erica is the botanical genus of heather

explanation.surface: A young woman sits beside the heather out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs, written M on scorecards; cricket is a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: America, the United States, is a nation.

clue.text: Claud gone squiffy? It's the French wine

indicators.note: squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk, so the letters stagger

explanation.surface: Is Claud tipsy? Blame the French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squiffy' (British slang for tipsy) rearranges CLAUD GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Languedoc is a southern French wine region whose wines take its name.
